href="https://downshiftology.com/recipes/berry-baked-oatmeal/">baked oatmeal</a>, <a href="https://downshiftology.com/recipes/egg-muffins/">egg muffins</a>, <a But let’s not overlook the humble bowl of oatmeal! While this healthy recipe may seem like a no brainer, many folks often search for the perfect recipe – <strong>one that creates a rich, creamy, and fluffy pot of oatmeal.</strong> Well, your search can stop here as I’ll show you how you can achieve the best bowl of oatmeal in a snap!</p>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-popular-types-of-oatmeal">Popular Types Of Oatmeal</h2>



<p>The texture of oatmeal can vary, depending on the type of oats you buy. Here are three popular varieties:</p>



<ul>
<li><strong>Steel Cut Oats:</strong> Steel-cut oats are whole oat groats chopped into pieces resembling little rice grains. They retain their shape well after cooking and results in a chewy and creamy like porridge. But, the cooking time is fairly long – about 30 minutes.</li>



<li><strong>Old Fashioned Rolled Oats:</strong> This type is <em>my favorite</em> to use for oatmeal! Rolled oats are steamed then rolled flat, which allows them to be cooked faster while still creating a deliciously creamy and hearty texture.</li>



<li><strong>Quick Cooking Oats:</strong> These are the most processed oats, undergoing pre-cooked, dried, rolled, and pressed steps. Their downside? They tend to produce a mushier oatmeal. But on the bright side, they only require about one minute to cook. So if you’re in a rush, this is a great option.</li>
</ul>

<h2 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-ingredients-for-the-best-oatmeal-recipe">Ingredients For The Best Oatmeal Recipe</h2>



<p>It takes just three ingredients to make the perfect bowl of oatmeal. Can’t beat that, eh?</p>



<ul>
<li><strong>Rolled Oats:</strong> These will create deliciously creamy porridge in just 5 to 10 minutes. Remember to buy certified gluten-free oats if you’re gluten-sensitive or celiac.</li>



<li><strong>Water or Milk:</strong> For the liquid you can use water, milk or dairy-free milk (like <a href="https://downshiftology.com/recipes/how-to-make-almond-milk/">almond milk</a> or <a href="https://downshiftology.com/how-to-make-cashew-milk/">cashew milk</a>), it’s up to you! For that perfect level of creaminess, a 50/50 water and milk combo is great.</li>



<li><strong>Salt:</strong> A pinch of salt will transform a bland bowl of oatmeal into a flavorful one. Trust me, don’t leave it out.</li>



<li><strong>Toppings:</strong> What’s oatmeal without toppings? Have fun with spices, fruits, nuts, and so much more (see below!)</li>
</ul>

<h2 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-is-oatmeal-gluten-free">Is Oatmeal Gluten Free?</h2>



<p>If you’re gluten intolerant or celiac (like me), you do need to be careful with what brand of oats you buy. While oats are naturally gluten-free, the facilities that process oats often process grains such as wheat, barley, or rye. And that creates significant grain “dust” which cross-contaminates the oats with gluten.</p>



<div id="AdThrive_Content_2_desktop" class="adthrive-ad adthrive-sticky-container adthrive-content adthrive-content-2 adthrive-ad-cls"></div><p>Additionally, the different types of crops are sometimes harvested with the same tools, leading to cross contamination. So it’s best to buy <strong>certified gluten-free oats</strong> to avoid any surprise flare ups.</p>
</div>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-how-to-make-oatmeal-like-a-pro">How To Make Oatmeal Like A Pro</h2>



<p>Just remember this <strong>ratio 1:2</strong>. For every portion of oats, you need <em>double</em> the amount of liquid. For a single serving with 1/2 cup of oats, that means you’ll need 1 cup of liquid.</p>

<h3 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-on-the-stove">On the Stove</h3>



<p>Whether you’re making a single portion or 10 portions for a crowd, it’s easy to make perfect oatmeal on the stove. Here’s the process:</p>



<ul>
<li><strong>Boil water.</strong> In a small pot, bring the water or milk and salt to a boil over medium-high heat.</li>



<li><strong>Cook the oats.</strong> Stir in the oats then reduce the heat to medium-low. Let it simmer for about 5 minutes to let the liquid absorb, while stirring occasionally.</li>



<li><strong>Top and serve.</strong> Add flavorful toppings, a drizzle of milk if you’d like, and enjoy.</li>
</ul>



<div id="AdThrive_Content_3_desktop" class="adthrive-ad adthrive-sticky-container adthrive-content adthrive-content-3 adthrive-ad-cls"></div><h3 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-in-the-microwave">In the Microwave</h3>



<p>This method is best for small or individual portions. Here’s the process:</p>



<ul>
<li><strong>Combine:</strong> The water or milk, oats, and salt in a bowl. Give it a quick stir.</li>



<li><strong>Heat:</strong> Microwave the bowl (uncovered) on high for 1 ½ to 2 minutes. The oats will start to bubble a bit, so it’s best to use a larger bowl.</li>



<li><strong>Top and serve:</strong> Again, you can add flavorful toppings, a drizzle of milk, maple syrup, etc., and enjoy.</li>
</ul>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-make-your-oatmeal-taste-amazing">Make Your Oatmeal Taste Amazing</h2>



<p>Popular toppings include maple syrup, spices, fresh fruit, dried fruit, nuts, seeds, and nut butters. Those are wonderful sweet toppings, but let’s not forget that oatmeal can be savory too! Think of oatmeal like a piece of toast (they’re both made from grains after all). So whatever you’d top on toast you can top on oatmeal!</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-sweet-flavors">Sweet Flavors</h3>



<ul>
<li><strong>Apple Cinnamon:</strong> Add diced apples, chopped pecans, a sprinkle of cinnamon, and a drizzle of maple syrup.</li>



<li><strong>Banana Blueberry:</strong> Add sliced bananas, blueberries, a drizzle of <a href="https://downshiftology.com/how-to-make-homemade-almond-butter/">almond butter</a>, and a sprinkle of chia seeds.</li>



<li><strong>Strawberries and Cream:</strong> Add diced strawberries, a dollop of <a href="https://downshiftology.com/recipes/how-to-make-homemade-yogurt/">yogurt</a>, and a sprinkle of flaxseeds.</li>



<li><strong>Raspberry Chia Jam:</strong> Add a spoonful of <a href="https://downshiftology.com/recipes/how-to-make-chia-seed-jam/">chia seed jam</a>, coconut flakes, sliced almonds, and extra milk on top.</li>



<li><strong>Chocolate Peanut Butter:</strong> Stir in cacao powder, then add a drizzle of peanut butter, and shredded coconut.</li>



<li><strong>Pumpkin Spice:</strong> Stir in pumpkin puree, pumpkin pie spice, vanilla extract, and top with chopped pecans and maple syrup.</li>



<li><strong>Coffee, Walnut & Dates:</strong> Replace some of the liquid with a little bit of brewed <a href="https://downshiftology.com/recipes/chemex-coffee-brewing/">coffee</a> as it’s cooking. Then top it off with chopped dates, toasted walnuts, and banana slices.</li>
</ul>

<h2 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-how-to-store-leftover-cooked-oatmeal">How To Store Leftover Cooked Oatmeal</h2>



<p>Did you make a little too much oatmeal? Or do you want to meal prep it? Well good news, you can save it and enjoy it throughout the week.</p>



<ul>
<li><strong>To store:</strong> Let the oatmeal cool, then place in a sealed container in the fridge for 3 to 5 days.</li>



<li><strong>For freezing:</strong> If you want to store it longer, just place it in the freezer. It will stay good for several months.</li>



<li><strong>To reheat:</strong> Add a splash of water or milk to revive its creaminess and microwave your bowl for about 45 seconds (if previously thawed in the fridge). Give it a stir, and pop it back in the microwave for one more minute until you’ve reached your desired temperature.</li>
</ul>

<h2 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-more-ways-to-use-oats">More Ways To Use Oats</h2>



<p>A bag of oats can take you much further than just a bowl of oatmeal. Here’s a few ways to get creative with them.</p>

<li>Blend some oats into creamy <a href="https://downshiftology.com/recipes/how-to-make-oat-milk/">oat milk</a>.</li>



<li>Mix with chocolate and bake them into the best <a href="https://downshiftology.com/recipes/no-bake-cookies/">no bake cookies</a>.</li>



<li>Create the best <a href="https://downshiftology.com/recipes/healthy-oatmeal-cookies/">oatmeal raisin cookies</a>!</li>

					<p>With the cold weather finally upon us here in Sonoma County (NorCal), we’re getting our oatmeal brekkies on. .wprm-recipe-template-cwp-food .wprm-call-to-action-text {
	font-size: 17px;
	line-height: 1.5;
	display: block;
}

.wprm-recipe-template-cwp-food .wprm-call-to-action-text::before {
	content: 'Leave a comment below and share a photo on Instagram. ';
}

.wprm-recipe-template-cwp-food .wprm-call-to-action.wprm-call-to-action-simple .wprm-call-to-action-icon {
	margin: 0 16px 0 0;
}


/* Save Recipe */

.cwp-food-save > .wpforms-container {
	background: var(--wp--preset--color--nonary);
	text-align: center;
	border: none;
	padding: 24px 16px;
	margin-top: 0;
	margin-bottom: 0;
}

.cwp-food-save .wpforms-container .wpforms-title {
	font-size: var(--wp--preset--font-size--x-large);
	margin-bottom: 8px;
}

.cwp-food-save .wpforms-container .wpforms-description {
	font-size: var(--wp--preset--font-size--small);
	text-transform: none;
	font-weight: normal;
	letter-spacing: 0;
}

.cwp-food-save .wpforms-container .wpforms-head-container > *:last-child {
	margin: 0;
}

.cwp-food-save .wpforms-container .wpforms-form,
.cwp-food-save .wpforms-container .wpforms-form > fieldset[disabled] {
	display: grid;
	grid-template-columns: 1fr fit-content(300px);
	row-gap: 24px;
}

.cwp-food-save .wpforms-container .wpforms-head-container {
	grid-column: 1 / -1;
}

.cwp-food-save .wpforms-container .wpforms-field-container {
	display: flex;
	gap: var(--wp--custom--layout--block-gap);
}

.cwp-food-save .wpforms-container .wpforms-field,
.cwp-food-save .wpforms-container .wpforms-field-large {
	margin: 0;
	flex-basis: 0;
	flex-grow: 1;
	height: 44px;
	border-radius: 0;
}

.cwp-food-save .wpforms-container .wpforms-field-label {
	min-height: 26px;
	text-align: left;
}

.cwp-food-save .wpforms-container .wpforms-submit-container {
	margin: 0;
}

@media only screen and (min-width: 768px) {

	.cwp-food-save div.wpforms-container .wpforms-form,
	.cwp-food-save div.wpforms-container.one-line .wpforms-form {
		grid-template-columns: 1fr fit-content(300px);
		align-items: flex-end;
	}

	.cwp-food-save div.wpforms-container .wpforms-head-container,
	.cwp-food-save div.wpforms-container.one-line .wpforms-head-container {
		grid-column: span 2;
	}
}
